issue: WireFailover (pre-start) and WireFailoverWithStop (post-start/G4) both assign the SAME `_engine._failover ??=` slot with differently-shaped restart delegates; whichever wires first wins for the engine lifetime (_failover is never nulled). Phase 5 calls WireFailover only when the pre-start config is dead (StartupPipeline.cs:1041); its delegate re-enters StartAsyncInternal directly with NO teardown, NO _lifecycleGate and under the caller token (VpnEngine.cs:1504). If that failover switches to a server that passes pre-start but fails the 15s post-start probe (or later restart-storms into G4), the post-start path calls WireFailoverWithStop (VpnEngine.cs:1593) but `??=` returns the already-wired pre-start delegate instead of ExecuteProbeFailoverRestartAsync. StartSingBoxPhaseAsync then news a SingBoxManager and overwrites _singBox via SetSingBoxManager (StartupPipeline.cs:1181-1184) without disposing the live one (TeardownInternal's _singBox.Dispose at VpnEngine.cs:794 is skipped) -> orphaned sing-box process + TUN adapter + leaked ProcessExit hook/TunOwnershipLock. The same ungated, probe-token bring-up also bypasses the _sessionCts resurrection guard, so a user Disconnect during it can revive the tunnel.
fix: Stop sharing one slot for two delegate shapes: have WireFailoverWithStop overwrite the restart delegate (or use a separate field) so post-start/G4 always route through ExecuteProbeFailoverRestartAsync; equivalently make the pre-start delegate teardown+gate via ExecuteProbeFailoverRestartAsync whenever _singBox.IsRunning(). Add a test: pre-start failover then post-start probe failure must dispose the prior SingBoxManager and never restart under a cancelled session.
